title: SpecOpt: Contact-Diff Reasoning for Agentic Molecule Optimization Toward Binding Specificity
abstract: arXiv:2609.21165v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Off-target protein binding is a major source of adverse effects for small-molecule drugs, yet most structure-based molecular design methods focus on generating selective compounds de novo rather than improving the selectivity of existing, well- characterized drugs. We introduce specificity optimization (SpecOpt), a molecular design task that seeks constrained structural modifications to an existing compound that increase its binding preference for an intended target over known off-targets while preserving its structural identity and drug-like properties. To enable systematic evaluation, we construct a ChEMBL-derived benchmark from compound-target interaction data, identifying intended targets through curated drug-mechanism annotations and off- targets through measured activities. translated_title: SpecOpt：面向结合特异性的智能体分子优化中的接触差异推理
translated_abstract: 脱靶蛋白结合是小分子药物不良反应的主要来源，然而大多数基于结构的分子设计方法专注于从头生成选择性化合物，而不是改进现有的、已被充分表征的药物的选择性。我们提出了特异性优化，这是一种分子设计任务，旨在寻找对现有化合物的受限结构修饰，以增加其对预期靶点相对于已知脱靶点的结合偏好，同时保持其结构特性和类药物性质。为了实现系统性评估，我们从化合物-靶点相互作用数据构建了一个基于ChEMBL的基准数据集，通过精心整理的药物机制注释识别预期靶点，并通过测量的活性识别脱靶点。随后，我们开发了一个智能体框架，将每个化合物与其预期靶点和脱靶点分别进行分子对接，并通过残基感知的方式比较所得到的结合姿态（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 提出SpecOpt任务与智能体框架，通过对现有药物进行受限结构修饰来提升其对预期靶点相对于脱靶点的结合特异性，并构建了基于ChEMBL的基准数据集以支持系统性评估。
en_tdlr: SpecOpt introduces a molecular design task and an agentic framework that applies constrained structural modifications to existing drugs to enhance binding specificity toward intended targets over off-targets, supported by a ChEMBL-derived benchmark for systematic evaluation.
